blocks.prompt: 1. Find the area of the region that is above the \(x\)-axis, but below the curve \(y = (x - 2)(3 - x)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh "area under the curve" wala sawal hai. Curve ek parabola hai jo neeche ki taraf khulta hai (ulta pyala), is liye yeh \(x\)-axis ke upar sirf apne do \(x\)-intercepts ke darmiyan hota hai.
Diya kya hai? Sirf curve \(y = (x - 2)(3 - x)\).
Find kya karna hai? Woh area jo \(x\)-axis ke upar aur curve ke neeche band hai.
Plan: pehle intercepts nikalenge (yehi limits banenge), phir check karenge ke darmiyan \(y\) positive hai, phir definite integral lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = (x - 2)(3 - x)\).
Maloom karna: \(x\)-axis ke upar aur curve ke neeche wala area.
Tareeqa: Area \(= \int_a^b y\,dx\), jahan \(a\) aur \(b\) woh points hain jahan curve axis ko kaatta hai, aur in ke darmiyan \(y \ge 0\) hai. Agar \(y\) positive ho to definite integral seedha area deta hai.

Qadam 1: \(x\)-intercepts nikalein
\[(x - 2)(3 - x) = 0\]
\[x = 2 \text{ ya } x = 3\]
Kyun: Region \(x\)-axis ko wahin chhoota hai jahan \(y = 0\) ho. Product zero tab hota hai jab koi ek factor zero ho, is liye \(x = 2\) ya \(x = 3\). Yehi do numbers hamari integration ki limits (hadein) hain.

Qadam 2: Darmiyan sign check karein
\(x = 2.5\) par: \(y = (0.5)(0.5) = 0.25 > 0\).
Kyun: Expand karein to \(y = -x^{2} + 5x - 6\); \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient negative hai, is liye parabola neeche khulta hai aur roots ke darmiyan axis ke upar rehta hai. Matlab integral positive aayega aur wohi area hoga.
Dhyan dein: Har dafa sign check karna zaroori hai; agar curve neeche hota to integral negative aata aur area ke liye us ka absolute value lena parta.

Qadam 3: Expand kar ke integrate karein
\[\int_2^3 (-x^{2} + 5x - 6)\,dx\]
\[= \left[-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{5x^{2}}{2} - 6x\right]_2^3\]
Kyun: Brackets khol kar polynomial bana liya, kyunke polynomial ko term by term power rule \(\int x^{n}dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\) se integrate karna sab se aasaan hai.

Qadam 4: Limits rakhein
\[F(3) = -9 + \dfrac{45}{2} - 18 = -\dfrac{9}{2}\]
\[F(2) = -\dfrac{8}{3} + 10 - 12 = -\dfrac{14}{3}\]
\[F(3) - F(2) = -\dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{14}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6}\]
Kyun: Fundamental theorem ke mutabiq upar wali limit ki value mein se neeche wali limit ki value minus karte hain. Fractions ko jama karne ke liye common denominator 6 liya: \(-\frac{27}{6} + \frac{28}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\).
Dhyan dein: \(F(2)\) negative hai, us ko minus karte waqt sign plus ban jata hai; yahan aksar ghalti hoti hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ek shortcut yaad rakhiye: parabola \(y = -(x - \alpha)(x - \beta)\) ke roots ke darmiyan area \(\frac{(\beta - \alpha)^{3}}{6}\) hota hai. Yahan \(\beta - \alpha = 3 - 2 = 1\), to area \(\frac{1}{6}\). Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab aaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.
